definition: A customer's commitment to use a supplier's chip or design service in a specific product generation. In custom silicon it starts a multi-year program but is not yet revenue.
A custom-chip model in which the design partner owns physical design, IP, packaging, test and foundry supply, and sells finished chips to the customer at a per-unit price.
A custom-chip model in which the customer does more of the design itself and buys only specific services or IP, then contracts the foundry directly; it lowers the partner's per-unit margin.

A separate die in a multi-chip package that handles input/output (memory controllers, SerDes, chip-to-chip links) so the compute die can use the leading-edge node. Design partners can supply only the I/O die.
A processor built specifically for neural-network math, usually with large matrix engines and less general-purpose control logic than a GPU. Huawei's Ascend and Qualcomm's Cloud AI parts are NPUs.

A chip design in which the compiler maps a model's operations onto a grid of compute and memory units and data streams between them, instead of a processor fetching instructions. SambaNova's RDU is an example.
A design that performs multiply-accumulate operations inside or right next to memory arrays, cutting the energy spent moving weights. d-Matrix's digital in-memory compute is an example.
A chip hard-wired for one model family, such as Etched's transformer-only Sohu. It can be very efficient if the architecture stays stable and becomes stranded if it changes.
A US Commerce Department list of foreign companies that need a licence to receive US-origin technology. Huawei, SMIC and several Chinese GPU designers are on it.

Printing features finer than a deep-ultraviolet scanner can resolve in one pass by exposing the same layer several times. It lets SMIC make 7 nm-class chips without EUV, at lower yield and higher cost.
China's policy of replacing foreign chips with local ones, for example by steering state-funded data centers to domestic AI accelerators.
Intel's 2025–26 process node with gate-all-around transistors (RibbonFET) and backside power delivery (PowerVia). It is the base of Intel's foundry pitch.
The general-purpose server CPU that schedules work, runs agent logic and feeds data to accelerators in an AI system. Qualcomm pitches its Dragonfly C1000 for this role.
A warrant that vests in tranches only as the holder buys a set dollar amount of the issuer's products; a supplier uses it to share upside with a large customer.
